symptom: PC1 (VLAN 10) cannot ping PC2, both on switch SW1, same subnet.
topology_note: SW1 Fa0/2->PC1, Fa0/3->PC2. Both should be VLAN 10.
show_output: SW1# show vlan brief | VLAN10 ACCTG active Fa0/2 | VLAN20 SALES active Fa0/3
expected_fault: Access port assigned to wrong VLAN (Fa0/3 is in VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10)

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 30 on SW2 cannot reach VLAN 30 hosts on SW1 across the trunk.
topology_note: SW1-SW2 connected via Gi0/1 trunk link.
show_output: SW1# show interfaces trunk | Port Gi0/1 Vlans allowed: 1,10,20 | Vlans allowed and active: 1,10,20
expected_fault: VLAN 30 not included in the trunk's allowed VLAN list

symptom: CDP native VLAN mismatch warnings on trunk link; occasional VLAN-30 traffic leaking to VLAN 1.
topology_note: SW1 Gi0/1 trunk to SW2 Gi0/1.
show_output: SW1# show interfaces trunk | Native vlan: 1 || SW2# show interfaces trunk | Native vlan: 99 | %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Gi0/1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch between trunk ends (SW1=1, SW2=99)

symptom: Router-on-a-stick sub-interface for VLAN 40 cannot get any ARP replies; PCs in VLAN 40 unreachable.
topology_note: R1 Gi0/0.40 encapsulation dot1Q 40, IP 192.168.40.1/24.
show_output: SW1# show vlan brief | (VLAN 40 not listed) || SW1# show run | interface vlan40 -> % Invalid input
expected_fault: VLAN 40 was never created on the switch (vlan database missing entry)

symptom: PC1 gets a valid IP via DHCP but cannot reach any host outside its own subnet.
show_output: PC1> ipconfig | Gateway: 192.168.1.100 || R1# show ip interface brief | Gi0/0 192.168.1.1 up up
expected_fault: PC1 configured with wrong default gateway (192.168.1.100 instead of .1)

symptom: All PCs in VLAN 20 lost gateway connectivity at the same time; gateway ping fails from every host.
topology_note: R1 sub-interface Gi0/0.20 is the VLAN 20 gateway.
show_output: R1# show ip interface brief | Gi0/0.20 192.168.20.1 administratively down down
expected_fault: Router sub-interface for VLAN 20 is administratively shut down

symptom: PC3 cannot ping its gateway even though the interface shows up/up on the router.
topology_note: PC3 gateway set to 192.168.30.254; router sub-interface uses .1.
show_output: R1# show run interface Gi0/0.30 | ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0 || PC3> ipconfig | Gateway: 192.168.30.254
expected_fault: Typo: PC3's configured gateway (.254) does not match the router's actual sub-interface IP (.1)

symptom: Intermittent gateway loss reported by two PCs; both show the same MAC in ARP for the gateway IP.
topology_note: 192.168.1.1 is meant to be only the router's SVI.
show_output: PC1> arp -a | 192.168.1.1 aaaa.bbbb.0001 || PC5> ipconfig | IP: 192.168.1.1 (statically set)
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address: PC5 was statically configured with the router's gateway address

symptom: New PCs joining VLAN 10 fail to obtain an IP address; existing PCs are fine.
topology_note: DHCP pool VLAN10 configured on R1 with a /27 network.
show_output: R1# show ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | Total addresses: 30 | Leased: 30 | Available: 0
expected_fault: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is exhausted (no addresses available)

symptom: PCs in VLAN 20 receive no IP address at all; DHCP server lives in VLAN 1 on R1.
topology_note: R1 Gi0/0.20 is the gateway for VLAN 20; DHCP pool is centrally hosted.
show_output: R1# show run interface Gi0/0.20 | ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0 (no ip helper-address line present)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 20 sub-interface to relay DHCP broadcasts

symptom: PCs in VLAN 30 receive IP addresses from the wrong subnet (192.168.99.x instead of 192.168.30.x).
topology_note: Pool named VLAN30 exists on R1.
show_output: R1# show run | ip dhcp pool VLAN30 -> network 192.168.99.0 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: DHCP pool VLAN30 is configured with the wrong network statement

symptom: Two devices intermittently report an IP conflict with the router's own gateway address.
topology_note: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 covers 192.168.10.0/24; gateway is .1.
show_output: R1# show run | ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.2 192.168.10.10 (missing .1)
expected_fault: DHCP excluded-address range does not include the gateway .1, so it gets leased out to a client

symptom: PCs can ping the file server by IP but 'ping server1.local' fails with 'Unknown host'.
topology_note: DHCP hands out DNS server address to clients.
show_output: PC2> ipconfig /all | DNS Servers: 192.168.1.250 (should be .200, the real DNS host)
expected_fault: DHCP option 6 (DNS server) is pointing at the wrong host IP

symptom: Name resolution fails intermittently; DNS server itself is reachable by ping but not by name queries.
topology_note: Extended ACL applied inbound on R1 Gi0/1 toward the DNS server subnet.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 101 | deny udp any any eq 53 (before any DNS permit line)
expected_fault: ACL 101 blocks UDP/53 (DNS) traffic before any permit statement is reached

symptom: Router-based DNS lookups fail for 'server1' when tested from the router itself; 'ip domain-lookup' is enabled.
topology_note: R1 configured to use a name server for troubleshooting via 'ping server1'.
show_output: R1# show run | ip domain-lookup | (no 'ip name-server' line present)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip name-server <dns-ip>' statement on the router

symptom: PC4 cannot resolve 'server1.local' even though DNS server config and reachability are correct for all other PCs.
topology_note: PC4 was recently moved from a lab subnet with a different DNS server.
show_output: PC4> ipconfig /all | DNS Servers: 10.10.10.10 (stale entry, statically set, not matching current network's DHCP-issued DNS)
expected_fault: PC4 has a stale statically-configured DNS entry left over from a previous network

symptom: VLAN 10 hosts cannot reach the 172.16.0.0/24 server subnet on R2; R1's routing table has no entry for it.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected via a point-to-point serial link, no dynamic routing configured.
show_output: R1# show ip route | 172.16.0.0 -- (no matching route line present)
expected_fault: Missing static route on R1 for the 172.16.0.0/24 network via R2

symptom: R1 and R2 are RIP neighbors, but hosts on R2's LAN cannot be reached from R1's LAN.
topology_note: RIP version 2 running between R1 and R2.
show_output: R2# show run | router rip | version 2 | network 10.0.0.0 (192.168.20.0 network statement missing)
expected_fault: R2 is not advertising its LAN network (192.168.20.0) into RIP

symptom: OSPF neighbor relationship between R1 and R2 stuck in INIT/EXSTART, no routes exchanged.
topology_note: Both routers configured for OSPF area on the shared link.
show_output: R1# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 | Area 0 || R2# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 | Area 1
expected_fault: OSPF area number mismatch between R1 (area 0) and R2 (area 1) on the shared link

symptom: Route to 172.16.20.0/24 exists in the routing table but traffic to it still times out.
topology_note: Static route configured pointing to a next-hop IP rather than an exit interface.
show_output: R1# show ip route 172.16.20.0 | via 172.16.10.2 || R1# show ip route 172.16.10.0 | (no directly connected or learned route to reach .2)
expected_fault: Recursive routing failure: the next-hop 172.16.10.2 is itself unreachable, so the static route never resolves

symptom: PCs in 192.168.10.0/24 can no longer reach the 192.168.30.0/24 server subnet after an ACL was added.
topology_note: Extended ACL 110 applied inbound on R1 Gi0/2.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 110 | 10 deny ip any any | (implicit/explicit deny-all is the only line, no permit statements)
expected_fault: ACL 110 has no permit statement for the 192.168.10.0/24 subnet, so all traffic is denied

symptom: ACL 120 was written to block only outbound Internet traffic from VLAN 40, but it is also blocking VLAN 40's inbound replies.
topology_note: ACL 120 applied on R1 Gi0/0.40.
show_output: R1# show run interface Gi0/0.40 | ip access-group 120 in (intended direction was out)
expected_fault: ACL 120 applied in the wrong direction (in instead of out) on the sub-interface

symptom: Host 192.168.10.15 should be blocked from the server subnet, but the whole 192.168.10.0/24 subnet lost access, including hosts that should be permitted.
topology_note: ACL 130 has a deny for the single host followed by a broader permit statement.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 130 | 10 deny ip host 192.168.10.15 any | 20 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any | 30 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL statement order denies the entire 192.168.10.0/24 subnet (line 20) instead of only the intended host

symptom: Internal clients can send requests to the web server, but replies never make it back to the clients.
topology_note: Extended ACL 140 applied inbound on the WAN-facing interface to protect the internal network.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 140 | 10 permit tcp any any eq 80 | (no 'established' or matching return-traffic permit for client-initiated sessions)
expected_fault: ACL 140 is missing a permit for established/return traffic, so reply packets from the server are dropped

symptom: All internal PCs can ping each other and the router, but none can reach the simulated Internet server.
topology_note: R1 has 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/1 overload' configured.
show_output: R1# show ip nat translations | (empty) || R1# show run | (no 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside' interface commands found)
expected_fault: NAT overload command exists, but the inside/outside interfaces were never marked, so no translation occurs

symptom: Only some internal hosts can reach the Internet server; others get no response at all.
topology_note: NAT overload references access-list 1 for the inside networks.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 1 | 10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 | (192.168.20.0 network not included)
expected_fault: NAT's referenced ACL only permits 192.168.10.0/24, leaving 192.168.20.0/24 untranslated

symptom: 'show ip nat translations' stays empty even though the NAT and ACL configuration both look correct.
topology_note: R1 Gi0/0 faces the LAN, Gi0/1 faces the simulated ISP.
show_output: R1# show ip nat statistics | Inside interfaces: (none) | Outside interfaces: (none)
expected_fault: Interfaces were never explicitly marked with 'ip nat inside' / 'ip nat outside'

symptom: External users cannot reach the internal web server via the public IP on port 80.
topology_note: Static NAT configured to publish an internal server to the outside.
show_output: R1# show run | ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.10.100 8080 203.0.113.10 80 (internal port mismatch: server actually listens on 80, not 8080)
expected_fault: Static NAT mapping references the wrong internal port (8080) instead of the server's actual port (80)

symptom: Laptop cannot associate with the corporate WLAN; repeated authentication failures.
topology_note: AP broadcasting SSID 'CORP-WIFI' with WPA2-PSK.
show_output: AP# show running-config | ssid CORP-WIFI | authentication key: Cisco123! || Laptop entered passphrase: cisco123
expected_fault: Passphrase mismatch between the client (lowercase, missing symbol) and the AP's configured key

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi clients can reach internal file servers and printers, which should never happen.
topology_note: Guest SSID mapped to VLAN 50; internal resources live in VLAN 10.
show_output: AP# show run | interface dot11radio0 | ssid GUEST-WIFI vlan 50 || SW1# show vlan brief | VLAN 50 not present; port defaults to VLAN 1 (same as internal trunk native)
expected_fault: Guest VLAN 50 was never created/trunked correctly, so guest traffic falls back onto the native/internal VLAN

symptom: Wireless clients near two APs experience high latency and frequent disconnects in the overlap zone.
topology_note: AP1 and AP2 cover adjoining rooms with overlapping coverage.
show_output: AP1# show interface dot11radio0 | Channel: 6 || AP2# show interface dot11radio0 | Channel: 6
expected_fault: Co-channel interference: both APs are set to the same 2.4GHz channel (6) in overlapping coverage areas

symptom: Wireless clients associate with the AP successfully but never receive an IP address.
topology_note: AP's wired uplink port on SW1 should trunk VLAN 60 (wireless clients) to R1 for DHCP relay.
show_output: SW1# show interfaces Fa0/5 switchport | Administrative Mode: static access | Access Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: AP's uplink switch port is set to access mode VLAN 1 instead of trunking VLAN 60 to the DHCP relay router
